newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan parties meet to discuss property.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan parties meet to discuss property.

text.p: Representatives of Nicaragua's government and the left-wing Sandinista opposition met on Thursday and agreed to form a joint commission to analyse each side's proposals for resolving Nicaragua's property problems.

It was the third meeting between the right-wing government of President Arnoldo Aleman and the Sandinistas to resolve the property conflicts left from the 1979-1990 Sandinista government, when the state confiscated thousands of private homes, farms and businesses.

At stake was the ownership of more than 200,000 of those properties the Sandinistas awarded themselves in a flurry of legislation before leaving office following their 1990 election loss to former President Violeta Chamorro.

Confounding predictions the dialogue would break off due to irreconcilable differences, the two sides talked for four hours with "calm and dignity," the head of the government delegation, Vice President Enrique Bolanos, told a news conference.
"We reached the conclusion that with all the revisions requested on the theme of property, we would agree to name a joint commission to go more into the specifics," Bolanos said.
The joint commission will have two members from each delegation and two weeks to analyse each side's proposals, Bolanos said.

The government delegation called for the revision of the legality of the confiscations carried out by the state during the Sandinista government, and for the Sandinistas to return all confiscated property they hold.

The Sandinista delegation in response called for a revision of the legality of properties acquired by officials in Nicaragua's last four governments, starting with former dictator Anastasio Somoza, who was toppled by the 1979 Sandinista revolution.

"An investigation should be done into the ill-gotten properties of the Somozas and unjust compensations paid to officials in the Somoza government," Congressman Bayardo Arce, the head of the Sandinista delegation, said.
